items.stem: Explain the term “formal charge”.
items.answer: The difference between the valence electrons of a free atom and the electrons assigned to it in a Lewis structure.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the difference between the valence electrons of a free atom and the electrons assigned to it in a Lewis structure.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about ionic and covalent bonding is correct?
items.answer: Noble gases like xenon form compounds such as XeF₂ and XeF₄.
items.markingKey: (c) Noble gases like xenon form compounds such as XeF₂ and XeF₄. The other statements are false. Boron in BF₃ has only six electrons (incomplete octet). Formal charges are a bookkeeping device; they do not show the real charge distribution. Lattice enthalpy increases with higher ionic charges and smaller ionic size.
options: In BF₃ boron has eight electrons around it.
Lattice enthalpy decreases with increase in the charges on the ions.
Noble gases like xenon form compounds such as XeF₂ and XeF₄.
Formal charges represent real charges on the atoms in a molecule.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a molecule with an expanded octet?
items.answer: BeCl₂
items.markingKey: (a) BeCl₂ is a molecule with an incomplete octet on the central atom, not a molecule with an expanded octet.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “In BF₃ boron has eight electrons around it.”
items.answer: Boron in BF₃ has only six electrons (incomplete octet).
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Boron in BF₃ has only six electrons (incomplete octet).

items.stem: Calculate the formal charge on the N atom in NO₃⁻.
items.markingKey: (c) Formal charge = V − L − ½B: 5 − 0 − ½(8) = +1.

items.stem: Although NaCl is formed from Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions, the formation of Na⁺(g) and Cl⁻(g) from atoms is endothermic overall. Why then does NaCl form so readily?
items.answer: The large lattice enthalpy released when gaseous ions come together to form the crystal more than compensates for the energy needed to form the ions.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: ion formation net endothermic (IE > |EGE|); 1 mark: lattice enthalpy makes the overall process exothermic.

items.stem: Which term describes a bond formed by the mutual sharing of a pair of electrons between two atoms?
items.answer: a covalent bond
items.markingKey: (d) A covalent bond: a bond formed by the mutual sharing of a pair of electrons between two atoms.

items.stem: Which of the following is an ionic compound?
items.answer: NaCl
items.markingKey: (c) NaCl is an ionic compound; the others are not.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as ionic compound or covalent compound: CH₄, CaF₂, MgO, KBr.
items.answer: CH₄ – covalent compound; CaF₂ – ionic compound; MgO – ionic compound; KBr – ionic compound.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: CH₄ – covalent compound; CaF₂ – ionic compound; MgO – ionic compound; KBr – ionic compound.

items.stem: Which of the following is a molecule with an incomplete octet on the central atom?
items.answer: BCl₃
items.markingKey: (c) BCl₃ is a molecule with an incomplete octet on the central atom; the others are not.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “The octet rule explains the stability of all molecules.”
items.answer: Many molecules (BF₃, PCl₅, NO) do not obey the octet rule.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Many molecules (BF₃, PCl₅, NO) do not obey the octet rule.

items.stem: Explain the term “dipole moment”.
items.answer: The product of the magnitude of the charge and the distance between the centres of positive and negative charge.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the product of the magnitude of the charge and the distance between the centres of positive and negative charge.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as non-polar molecule or polar molecule: NF₃, BeF₂, CCl₄, HCl.
items.answer: NF₃ – polar molecule; BeF₂ – non-polar molecule; CCl₄ – non-polar molecule; HCl – polar molecule.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: NF₃ – polar molecule; BeF₂ – non-polar molecule; CCl₄ – non-polar molecule; HCl – polar molecule.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a non-polar molecule?
items.answer: H₂O
items.markingKey: (c) H₂O is a polar molecule, not a non-polar molecule.

items.stem: What is the average bond order of the bonds in benzene (C–C)?
items.markingKey: (c) 1.5: two Kekulé structures give each C–C bond half double-bond character.

items.stem: In a diatomic molecule the partial charges are ±0.6e and the bond length is 160 pm. Calculate the dipole moment in debye. (e = 1.602 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, 1 D = 3.336 × 10⁻³⁰ C m)
Use resonance to explain why both O–O bonds in ozone have the same length (128 pm), intermediate between O–O (148 pm) and O=O (121 pm).
items.answer: O₃ is a resonance hybrid of two structures with the double bond in either position; each O–O bond has bond order 1.5, so both lengths are equal and intermediate.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: two canonical forms; 1 mark: bond order 1.5 ⇒ equal, intermediate length.

items.stem: Which of the following is a non-polar molecule?
items.answer: BeF₂
items.markingKey: (a) BeF₂ is a non-polar molecule; the others are not.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “A triple bond is longer than a double bond between the same two atoms.”
items.answer: A triple bond is shorter than a double bond.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: A triple bond is shorter than a double bond.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): The canonical forms of a molecule have no real existence.
Reason (R): The canonical structures of a molecule exist in equilibrium with each other.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: Canonical forms have no real existence; the molecule is a single resonance hybrid.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Define the term “resonance”.
items.answer: The representation of a molecule by two or more Lewis structures, none of which alone describes it fully.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the representation of a molecule by two or more Lewis structures, none of which alone describes it fully.

items.stem: What is meant by “a bond pair”?
items.answer: A pair of electrons shared between two atoms.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a pair of electrons shared between two atoms.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about VSEPR theory is correct?
items.answer: In SF₄ the lone pair occupies an equatorial position.
items.markingKey: (a) In SF₄ the lone pair occupies an equatorial position. The other statements are false. XeF₂ is linear: three lone pairs occupy the equatorial positions of a trigonal bipyramid. It is 104.5° because two lone pairs compress the angle. Lone pair–lone pair repulsion is the strongest.
options: In SF₄ the lone pair occupies an equatorial position.
Bond pair–bond pair repulsion is the strongest of all repulsions.
The H–O–H bond angle in water is 109.5°.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): In SF₄ the lone pair occupies an equatorial position.
Reason (R): XeF₂ is bent like H₂O.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: XeF₂ is linear: three lone pairs occupy the equatorial positions of a trigonal bipyramid.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “The H–O–H bond angle in water is 109.5°.”
items.answer: It is 104.5° because two lone pairs compress the angle.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: It is 104.5° because two lone pairs compress the angle.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about VSEPR theory is incorrect?
items.answer: XeF₂ is bent like H₂O.
items.markingKey: (a) The incorrect statement is “XeF₂ is bent like H₂O.” Correct form: XeF₂ is linear: three lone pairs occupy the equatorial positions of a trigonal bipyramid.
options: In SF₄ the lone pair occupies an equatorial position.
XeF₄ is square planar with two lone pairs on Xe.

items.stem: Which of the following has the same shape as XeF₂?
items.answer: I₃⁻
items.markingKey: (c) XeF₂ and I₃⁻ are both linear; PCl₅ is trigonal bipyramidal; SO₃ is trigonal planar; SF₆ is octahedral.

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct decreasing order of repulsion between electron pairs: bond pair–bond pair, lone pair–lone pair, lone pair–bond pair. Give a reason.
items.answer: lone pair–lone pair > lone pair–bond pair > bond pair–bond pair
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the order lone pair–lone pair > lone pair–bond pair > bond pair–bond pair; 1 mark for the reason: Lone pairs are held by only one nucleus and spread out more, so they repel more strongly.

items.stem: Both BF₃ and NH₃ are AB₃ molecules, but BF₃ is planar and NH₃ is pyramidal. Explain using VSEPR theory.
items.answer: B in BF₃ has 3 bond pairs and no lone pair ⇒ trigonal planar. N in NH₃ has 3 bond pairs and 1 lone pair ⇒ tetrahedral electron geometry with pyramidal shape.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each for correct electron-pair count and shape.

items.stem: Using VSEPR theory, predict the shapes of (a) SF₄, (b) ClF₃, (c) XeF₂, (d) BrF₅ and (e) XeF₄. For each, state the number of bond pairs and lone pairs on the central atom.
items.answer: (a) 4 bp, 1 lp – see-saw. (b) 3 bp, 2 lp – T-shaped. (c) 2 bp, 3 lp – linear. (d) 5 bp, 1 lp – square pyramidal. (e) 4 bp, 2 lp – square planar.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each (pairs and shape).

items.stem: According to VSEPR theory, what is the shape of BrF₅?
items.answer: square pyramidal
items.markingKey: (d) BrF₅: 5 bond pairs + 1 lone pair(s) around the central atom ⇒ square pyramidal (about 84.5°).

items.stem: What is meant by “a lone pair”?
items.answer: A pair of electrons on an atom that is not shared.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a pair of electrons on an atom that is not shared.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “XeF₂ is bent like H₂O.”
items.answer: XeF₂ is linear: three lone pairs occupy the equatorial positions of a trigonal bipyramid.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: XeF₂ is linear: three lone pairs occupy the equatorial positions of a trigonal bipyramid.

items.stem: Define the term “a pi (π) bond”.
items.answer: A bond formed by sidewise overlap of p orbitals with axes parallel to each other.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a bond formed by sidewise overlap of p orbitals with axes parallel to each other.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about hybridisation is correct?
items.answer: Hybrid orbitals form only σ bonds.
items.markingKey: (a) Hybrid orbitals form only σ bonds. The other statements are false. A π bond is always formed in addition to a σ bond. Axial P–Cl bonds (240 pm) are longer than equatorial ones (202 pm). sp³ has 25% and sp² has 33.3% s character.
options: Hybrid orbitals form only σ bonds.
In PCl₅ all five P–Cl bonds are of equal length.
A π bond can be formed without a σ bond between two atoms.
sp³ orbitals have more s character than sp² orbitals.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Free rotation is possible about a C–C single bond but not about a C=C double bond.
Reason (R): Hybrid orbitals form π bonds.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: Hybrid orbitals form σ bonds; π bonds come from unhybridised p orbitals.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: A central atom has the following hybridisation features: found in PCl₅; five hybrid orbitals; three equatorial and two axial positions. Identify the type of hybridisation. Give a reason.
items.answer: Sp³d
items.markingKey: 1 mark: sp³d; 1 mark: the features found in PCl₅; five hybrid orbitals; three equatorial and two axial positions are characteristic of it.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): PCl₅ is very reactive.
Reason (R): The two axial P–Cl bonds are longer and weaker than the equatorial bonds.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Weaker axial bonds break easily, making PCl₅ reactive.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Number the carbon atoms from left to right in HC≡C–CH=CH₂ and state the hybridisation of each.
items.answer: C1: sp, C2: sp, C3: sp², C4: sp²
items.markingKey: Four σ (single bonds only) ⇒ sp³; one double bond ⇒ sp²; one triple or two double bonds ⇒ sp: C1: sp, C2: sp, C3: sp², C4: sp². (½ mark each)

items.stem:
A central atom has the following hybridisation features: uses two d orbitals; found in SF₆; octahedral arrangement.
(i) Identify the type of hybridisation. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were sp³d? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Sp³d² (ii) six hybrid orbitals at 90° (iii) three equatorial and two axial positions; found in PCl₅
items.markingKey: (i) sp³d² – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: six hybrid orbitals at 90° – 1 mark. (iii) for sp³d: five hybrid orbitals; three equatorial and two axial positions; found in PCl₅ – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct increasing order of electronegativity of carbon: sp² carbon, sp³ carbon, sp carbon. Give a reason.
items.answer: sp³ carbon < sp² carbon < sp carbon
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the order sp³ carbon < sp² carbon < sp carbon; 1 mark for the reason: More s character holds electrons closer to the nucleus.

items.stem: How many σ and π bonds are present in acrylonitrile (CH₂=CH–C≡N)?
items.answer: 6 σ and 3 π
items.markingKey: Every single bond is one σ; a double bond is 1σ + 1π; a triple bond is 1σ + 2π ⇒ 6 σ, 3 π.

items.stem: Describe the hybridisation in the formation of ethene. Show how the σ and π bonds are formed, and explain why ethene is planar and does not show free rotation about the C=C bond.
items.answer: Each C is sp² (2s + 2pₓ + 2p_y); two sp² orbitals overlap with H 1s, one with the other C (σ C–C). The unhybridised 2p_z orbitals overlap sideways to form the π bond. All σ bonds lie in one plane (120°); rotation would break the sideways π overlap.
items.markingKey: 1 mark sp² hybridisation; 1 mark σ framework; 1 mark π bond from p_z; 1 mark planarity; 1 mark no free rotation.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “The overlap of a 1s and a 2p orbital always gives a π bond.”
items.answer: s–p head-on overlap gives a σ bond.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: s–p head-on overlap gives a σ bond.

items.stem: Number the carbon atoms from left to right in CH₃–CHO and state the hybridisation of each.
items.answer: C1: sp³, C2: sp²
items.markingKey: Four σ (single bonds only) ⇒ sp³; one double bond ⇒ sp²; one triple or two double bonds ⇒ sp: C1: sp³, C2: sp². (½ mark each)

items.stem: A central atom has the following hybridisation features: trigonal bipyramidal arrangement; five hybrid orbitals. Identify the type of hybridisation.
items.answer: sp³d
items.markingKey: (d) Sp³d: trigonal bipyramidal arrangement; five hybrid orbitals.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between sp³d and sp³ on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A central atom has the following hybridisation features: 25% s character. Identify the type of hybridisation – sp³d or sp³? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Sp³d: five hybrid orbitals; three equatorial and two axial positions; found in PCl₅. Sp³: four hybrid orbitals at 109.5°; 25% s character; found in CH₄ and C₂H₆. (b) Sp³.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: sp³; 1 mark: “25% s character” is a feature of sp³.

items.stem: Define the term “a hydrogen bond”.
items.answer: The attractive force that binds a hydrogen atom of one molecule (or group) to a highly electronegative atom of another.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the attractive force that binds a hydrogen atom of one molecule (or group) to a highly electronegative atom of another.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as compound showing intermolecular hydrogen bonding or compound showing intramolecular hydrogen bonding: salicylaldehyde (o-hydroxybenzaldehyde), o-hydroxybenzoic acid, hydrogen fluoride, o-nitrophenol.
items.answer: salicylaldehyde (o-hydroxybenzaldehyde) – compound showing intramolecular hydrogen bonding; o-hydroxybenzoic acid – compound showing intramolecular hydrogen bonding; hydrogen fluoride – compound showing intermolecular hydrogen bonding; o-nitrophenol – compound showing intramolecular hydrogen bonding.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: salicylaldehyde (o-hydroxybenzaldehyde) – compound showing intramolecular hydrogen bonding; o-hydroxybenzoic acid – compound showing intramolecular hydrogen bonding; hydrogen fluoride – compound showing intermolecular hydrogen bonding; o-nitrophenol – compound showing intramolecular hydrogen bonding.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a compound showing intermolecular hydrogen bonding?
items.answer: methane
items.markingKey: (d) Methane is a substance with no hydrogen bonding, not a compound showing intermolecular hydrogen bonding.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Hydrogen bonds are stronger than covalent bonds.”
items.answer: Hydrogen bonds are much weaker than covalent bonds.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Hydrogen bonds are much weaker than covalent bonds.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about molecular orbital theory and hydrogen bonding is incorrect?
items.answer: o-Nitrophenol has a higher boiling point than p-nitrophenol.
items.markingKey: (b) The incorrect statement is “o-Nitrophenol has a higher boiling point than p-nitrophenol.” Correct form: o-Nitrophenol has intramolecular H-bonding and is more volatile; p-nitrophenol has intermolecular H-bonding and a higher boiling point.
options: A bond order of zero means the molecule is not stable.
o-Nitrophenol has a higher boiling point than p-nitrophenol.
Intermolecular hydrogen bonding raises the boiling point.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): O₂ is paramagnetic.
Reason (R): O₂ has two unpaired electrons in its antibonding π*2p orbitals.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Unpaired electrons make O₂ paramagnetic.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Ethanol (46 g mol⁻¹) boils at 351 K but dimethyl ether (46 g mol⁻¹) boils at 248 K. Explain.
items.answer: Ethanol molecules are associated by intermolecular hydrogen bonds (O–H…O), which need extra energy to break; dimethyl ether has no O–H and cannot H-bond with itself.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: H-bonding in ethanol; 1 mark: none in ether.

items.stem: Arrange O₂²⁻, O₂, O₂⁻, O₂⁺ in increasing order of bond order and hence of stability. Show the bond orders.
items.answer: O₂²⁻ < O₂⁻ < O₂ < O₂⁺
items.markingKey: Bond orders: O₂²⁻ 1, O₂⁻ 1.5, O₂ 2, O₂⁺ 2.5 ⇒ O₂²⁻ < O₂⁻ < O₂ < O₂⁺. Higher bond order means greater stability and shorter bond.

items.stem: Which of the following is a compound showing intermolecular hydrogen bonding?
items.answer: hydrogen fluoride
items.markingKey: (d) Hydrogen fluoride is a compound showing intermolecular hydrogen bonding; the others are not.

items.stem: Which term describes a molecular orbital formed by additive overlap of atomic orbitals, with electron density increased between the nuclei?
items.answer: a bonding molecular orbital
items.markingKey: (c) A bonding molecular orbital: a molecular orbital formed by additive overlap of atomic orbitals, with electron density increased between the nuclei.

items.stem: Using molecular orbital theory, calculate the bond order of F₂ and predict whether it is paramagnetic or diamagnetic.
items.answer: Bond order 1; diamagnetic
items.markingKey: 18 electrons: (σ1s)² (σ*1s)² (σ2s)² (σ*2s)² (σ2p)² (π2p)⁴ (π*2p)⁴ (1); bond order = (N_b − N_a)/2 = (10 − 8)/2 = 1 (½); 0 unpaired electron(s) ⇒ diamagnetic (½).

items.stem: (a) Write the molecular orbital configuration of N₂ and O₂. (b) Calculate their bond orders. (c) Explain why O₂ is paramagnetic but N₂ is diamagnetic. (d) Predict which of N₂ and N₂⁺ has the longer bond.
items.answer: (a) N₂: σ1s² σ*1s² σ2s² σ*2s² π2p⁴ σ2p²; O₂: … σ2p² π2p⁴ π*2p². (b) N₂ 3, O₂ 2. (c) O₂ has two unpaired π* electrons; N₂ has none. (d) N₂⁺ (bond order 2.5) has the longer bond.
items.markingKey: (a) 2 marks (b) 1 mark (c) 1 mark (d) 1 mark.

items.stem: What is the hybridisation of the carbonyl carbon in CH₃COOH?
items.answer: sp²
items.markingKey: (d) Count σ bonds + lone pairs on the atom: sp².

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct increasing order of dipole moment: CCl₄, H₂O, NF₃, NH₃. Give a reason.
items.answer: CCl₄ < NF₃ < NH₃ < H₂O

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Hybrid orbitals form π bonds.”
items.answer: Hybrid orbitals form σ bonds; π bonds come from unhybridised p orbitals.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Hybrid orbitals form σ bonds; π bonds come from unhybridised p orbitals.

items.stem: Which term describes the theory that a covalent bond forms by overlap of half-filled atomic orbitals of the bonding atoms?
items.answer: valence bond theory
items.markingKey: (d) Valence bond theory: the theory that a covalent bond forms by overlap of half-filled atomic orbitals of the bonding atoms.

items.stem:
A central atom has the following hybridisation features: four hybrid orbitals at 109.5°; tetrahedral arrangement; 25% s character.
(i) Identify the type of hybridisation. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were sp³d? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Sp³ (ii) found in CH₄ and C₂H₆ (iii) trigonal bipyramidal arrangement; three equatorial and two axial positions
items.markingKey: (i) sp³ – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: found in CH₄ and C₂H₆ – 1 mark. (iii) for sp³d: five hybrid orbitals; three equatorial and two axial positions; found in PCl₅ – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about molecular orbital theory and hydrogen bonding is correct?
items.answer: N₂ has a bond order of 3.
items.markingKey: (c) N₂ has a bond order of 3. The other statements are false. O₂ has two unpaired electrons in π*2p orbitals and is paramagnetic. o-Nitrophenol has intramolecular H-bonding and is more volatile; p-nitrophenol has intermolecular H-bonding and a higher boiling point. O₂⁺ has bond order 2.5, greater than O₂ (2).
options: Bond order of O₂⁺ is less than that of O₂.
O₂ is diamagnetic because all its electrons are paired.
N₂ has a bond order of 3.
o-Nitrophenol has a higher boiling point than p-nitrophenol.

items.stem: How many bond pairs and lone pairs are there around the central atom of BrF₅? Predict its shape.
items.answer: 5 bond pairs, 1 lone pair; square pyramidal
items.markingKey: Count the valence electrons of the central atom used in σ bonds and left over: 5 bp + 1 lp ⇒ electron geometry of 6 pairs; shape square pyramidal (1 + 1).

items.stem: What is the hybridisation of the N atom in NH₃?
items.answer: sp³
items.markingKey: (b) Count σ bonds + lone pairs on the atom: sp³.

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct increasing order of bond length: H–Cl, H–I, H–F, H–Br. Give a reason.
items.answer: H–F < H–Cl < H–Br < H–I
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the order H–F < H–Cl < H–Br < H–I; 1 mark for the reason: Halogen atom size increases from F to I.

items.stem: Which of the following shows the correct decreasing order of bond angle?
items.answer: BeCl₂ > BF₃ > CH₄ > NH₃

items.stem: Explain the term “a paramagnetic substance”.
items.answer: A substance that is attracted by a magnetic field because it has unpaired electrons.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a substance that is attracted by a magnetic field because it has unpaired electrons.

items.stem: A central atom has the following hybridisation features: trigonal bipyramidal arrangement; three equatorial and two axial positions; five hybrid orbitals. Identify the type of hybridisation. Give a reason.
items.answer: Sp³d
items.markingKey: 1 mark: sp³d; 1 mark: the features trigonal bipyramidal arrangement; three equatorial and two axial positions; five hybrid orbitals are characteristic of it.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Formation of an ionic bond is favoured by low ionisation enthalpy of the metal and highly negative electron gain enthalpy of the non-metal.
Reason (R): In BF₃ boron has eight electrons around it.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: Boron in BF₃ has only six electrons (incomplete octet).
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct increasing order of covalent character: MgCl₂, AlCl₃, NaCl. Give a reason.
items.answer: NaCl < MgCl₂ < AlCl₃
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the order NaCl < MgCl₂ < AlCl₃; 1 mark for the reason: By Fajans' rules, higher charge and smaller cation polarise the anion more.

items.stem: What is the average bond order of the bonds in CO₃²⁻?
items.markingKey: (c) 1.33: three resonance structures share one double bond among three C–O bonds.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT an ionic compound?
items.answer: H₂O
items.markingKey: (c) H₂O is a covalent compound, not an ionic compound.

items.stem: Which term describes the arrangement in space of all electron pairs (bond and lone) around the central atom?
items.answer: electron-pair geometry
items.markingKey: (a) Electron-pair geometry: the arrangement in space of all electron pairs (bond and lone) around the central atom.

items.stem: How many σ and π bonds are present in propene (CH₃–CH=CH₂)?
items.answer: 8 σ and 1 π
items.markingKey: Every single bond is one σ; a double bond is 1σ + 1π; a triple bond is 1σ + 2π ⇒ 8 σ, 1 π.

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct decreasing order of repulsion between electron pairs: lone pair–lone pair, bond pair–bond pair, lone pair–bond pair. Give a reason.
items.answer: lone pair–lone pair > lone pair–bond pair > bond pair–bond pair
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the order lone pair–lone pair > lone pair–bond pair > bond pair–bond pair; 1 mark for the reason: Lone pairs are held by only one nucleus and spread out more, so they repel more strongly.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a non-polar molecule?
items.answer: SO₂
items.markingKey: (c) SO₂ is a polar molecule, not a non-polar molecule.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “In PCl₅ all five P–Cl bonds are of equal length.”
items.answer: Axial P–Cl bonds (240 pm) are longer than equatorial ones (202 pm).
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Axial P–Cl bonds (240 pm) are longer than equatorial ones (202 pm).

items.stem: Which term describes a bond formed by end-to-end (head-on) overlap of orbitals along the internuclear axis?
items.answer: a sigma (σ) bond
items.markingKey: (c) A sigma (σ) bond: a bond formed by end-to-end (head-on) overlap of orbitals along the internuclear axis.
